challenges.title: post { always }
challenges.description: A declarative Jenkinsfile ends with: post { always { junit 'reports/*.xml' } }
challenges.instructions: Why put the junit step in post { always }?
hints: Failed builds are when you most need the report.
post conditions run after the stages.
challenges.explanation:
post { always } runs whatever the build result. Publishing JUnit results there means failing builds still
       show which tests failed and keep the trend charts complete.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 12 Jenkinsfile Engineering; Ch. 15
options: So test results are published even when the test stage fails

challenges.title: Order the pipeline stages
challenges.instructions: Order the stages from first to last.
hints: You need the code before you can install anything.
Fast checks run before slow ones.
challenges.explanation:
Checkout first, then a reproducible environment, then cheap static checks that fail fast, then the
            tests, and finally reporting, which should run even after failures.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Project 1 Python Test Automation CI Pipeline
steps: Create a virtual environment and install pinned dependencies
Publish JUnit results and archive logs

challenges.title: The leaking credential
challenges.description: This stage works, but the security review flags it.
hints: Who expands ${...} in a double-quoted Groovy string?
Jenkins warns about insecure interpolation of secrets.
challenges.explanation:
In double quotes Groovy substitutes the values before the shell runs, so the password becomes part of the
        command string, where it can leak into process lists and logs. Use sh 'curl -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" ...'
        so the shell reads the environment variables. (-k also disables TLS checks; prefer a CA bundle.)
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 19 Jenkins Credentials and Security
options: The double-quoted Groovy string interpolates the secret into the command text; use single quotes so the shell expands it
withCredentials cannot be used inside a stage

challenges.title: Green locally, red in CI
challenges.description: After a merge, the pipeline fails on import errors that nobody can reproduce locally.
challenges.instructions: What is the most likely cause?
hints: What does pip install -r requirements.txt pick without version pins?
The agent installs fresh.
challenges.explanation:
Without pinned versions or a lock file, a fresh CI install can pull a newer release with breaking changes.
       Pin versions, use the same Python version, and consider building in a container for reproducibility.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 21 Containers and Reproducible CI Environments
options: Unpinned dependencies resolved to different versions on the CI agent
The developer's laptop has more RAM

challenges.title: pytest exit codes
challenges.description: A pipeline step decides whether to mark the build UNSTABLE or FAILED based on pytest's exit code.
challenges.instructions: Fill the blank with the exit code pytest uses when tests ran and some failed.
hints: 0 means all passed.
2 means interrupted, 5 means no tests collected.
challenges.explanation:
pytest returns 0 when all tests pass, 1 when some fail, 2 when interrupted, 3 on internal error, 4 on usage
         error and 5 when no tests were collected. Treating 5 as success is a classic CI mistake.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 14 Python Test Execution in CI
challenges.code: pytest exits with code ____ when tests were collected and run but some failed.

challenges.title: 115200 8N1
challenges.description: A board's console is documented as 115200 8N1.
hints: The order is data bits, parity, stop bits.
N stands for none.
challenges.explanation:
8N1 is the most common UART frame: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, at 115200 baud. Both ends must
       match exactly.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook · UART chapter; Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · UART debugging
options: 8 stop bits, no data bits, 1 parity bit
8 data bits, no parity bit, 1 stop bit

challenges.title: Embedded Linux boot chain
challenges.description: A BMC hangs during boot and you need to know which stage it reached.
challenges.instructions: Order the boot stages of a typical embedded Linux system.
hints: Hardware ROM code runs first.
Services need a mounted root filesystem.
challenges.explanation:
Knowing the chain tells you where to look: a hang with no U-Boot banner is pre-bootloader, a panic after
            "Starting kernel" is kernel or rootfs, and a hang after systemd starts is a service issue.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Ch. 1.6 Boot process; kernel & boot debugging
steps: Bootloader loads the kernel and device tree
Kernel initialises drivers and mounts the root filesystem

challenges.title: Garbled console
challenges.description: The serial console prints random symbols like Ã¿ø÷ instead of boot messages.
challenges.instructions: What is the most likely cause?
hints: Data arrives, but it decodes wrongly.
Check the timing settings first.
challenges.explanation:
Consistent garbage almost always means the terminal samples at a different baud rate than the board
       transmits. Confirm the documented rate (often 115200) and the 8N1 frame before suspecting firmware.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · UART debugging; API & Protocol Automation Handbook · UART
options: Baud rate mismatch between the terminal and the board
The USB cable is too short

challenges.title: Version 2.10 is older?
challenges.description: A firmware gate rejects version 2.10, which should satisfy the minimum 2.9.
hints: Compare "1" and "9" after "2."
Split on dots and convert parts to int.
challenges.explanation:
String comparison is lexicographic: at the third character "1" < "9", so "2.10" < "2.9". Compare
        tuple(int(p) for p in v.split(".")) or use packaging.version.Version. Converting to float also fails
        (2.10 becomes 2.1).
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Project P10 Firmware-Version Validation
options: The function must print the result
Version strings are compared character by character, so "2.10" < "2.9"; compare numeric tuples

challenges.title: Unable to mount root fs
challenges.description: After a firmware update, the console ends with: Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs.
hints: The kernel started but could not find or read its root filesystem.
Who tells the kernel where root is?
challenges.explanation:
The kernel booted, so the bootloader worked, but it could not mount the root filesystem. Check that the
       rootfs image was written correctly, that root= and rootfstype in the bootargs match the new layout, and that
       the driver for the storage is built in.
challenges.source: Linux, Bash & Embedded Debugging Handbook · Kernel and boot debugging; Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 26 CI Failure Analysis
options: The root filesystem image or partition, and the root= boot arguments passed by the bootloader
